claim: A single unlocked CMP 170HX measured 1.69 GB/s per direction at PCIe Gen2 x4 after a reseat, versus 0.84 GB/s at Gen1 x4 before it.
stance_target: the repo's 'PCIe Gen2 x4' premise, and corroborates bayley/cmpunlocker's 1.68 GB/s BAR1-P2P figure on the same link generation and width
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX, 64 GiB HBM2e, ~1.49 TB/s, 150-300 W, blower on a temperature-driven curve; runs before 2026-09-10 at Gen1 x4, after a reseat at Gen2 x4
quoted_support: PCIe trained at Gen1 x4 (0.84 GB/s) for runs before 2026-09-10, Gen2 x4 (1.69 GB/s) after a reseat.

claim: Median decode throughput on this card retains 93.5% of its 1k-context rate at 32k context, 88.1% at 64k and 79.4% at 128k, measured across 75 models/engines per depth to 64k and 56 at 128k.
stance_target: the premise that long-context attention cost is the binding constraint at 32k on this card — dense attention costs only ~6.5% of decode throughput at 32k, so a compressed-sparse-attention scheme must beat a ~6.5% penalty plus its own indexer overhead to pay off
scope_conditions: One unlocked CMP 170HX at 300 W, speculation off, vLLM/llama.cpp/SGLang, 1,603 decode points across 16 models, depths 1k-128k; median retained rate across every model and engine that ran both that depth and the 1k reference

claim: A matched SGLang ladder re-run after the link changed from Gen1 x4 to Gen2 x4 reproduced every prompt depth within 0.3%, so single-card decode is essentially link-insensitive.
stance_target: how much of the box's behaviour is fabric-limited — single-card work is not, so fabric cost only appears in multi-card collectives
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX, SGLang, matched ladder across the link change, depths 1k-128k
quoted_support: A matched SGLang ladder on the new link reproduced every depth within 0.3%.

claim: The power-limit ladder across 210 matched measurements shows 250 W retaining 99.3% of the 300 W decode rate, 200 W retaining 95.7% and 150 W retaining 85.2%.
stance_target: the power/throughput trade-off available for a five-card training run — running at 250 W costs almost nothing in throughput
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX, every ladder point repeated at 300/250/200/150 W, speculation off

claim: Speculative decoding gains decay with context depth: DFlash falls from 2.22x at 1k to 1.22x at 128k, MTP from 1.88x to 0.76x (the drafter costs more than it returns at 128k), and DSpark from 2.06x to 1.40x.
stance_target: whether speculative decoding is a usable throughput lever at long context — it is not at 128k, and it degrades materially by 32k
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX at 300 W, speculation off baseline, median gain by depth
quoted_support: | DFlash  | 2.22×  | 2.02×  | 2.01×  | 1.79×  | 1.56×  | 1.22×  | | MTP  | 1.88×  | 1.90×  | 1.61×  | 1.42×  | 1.28×  | 0.76×  | ... MTP is 0.76× at 128k, so the drafter costs more than it returns at that depth.

claim: At 32k context on one card, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B W4A16 on vLLM scales from 237 tok/s aggregate at n=1 to 1,306 tok/s at n=16, with TTFT rising from 3.3 s to 31.0 s and KV occupancy from 0.6% to 9.9%.
stance_target: the single-card throughput and KV-footprint envelope at 32k, which is the context length the CSA2 question is asked about
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX at 300 W, vLLM, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B W4A16, 32k prompts, 256-token outputs, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85

claim: W4A16 quantisation on this card costs 1.3 points of HumanEval pass@1 versus bf16 (0.927 vs 0.939) and 8.7 points of GSM8K strict-match (0.444 vs 0.532), so quantised runs are not quality-equivalent to bf16.
stance_target: whether quantised training or eval experiments on this box can be compared to bf16 baselines — the quantisation gap is large enough on some benchmarks to confound comparisons
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-27B on one CMP 170HX; HumanEval n=164, GSM8K n=1,319, IFEval n=541; few-shot completion prompts built for base models
quoted_support: | HumanEval pass@1  | 164  | 0.939  | 0.939  | 0.927  | −1.3%  | ... | GSM8K strict  | 1,319  | 0.532  | 0.532  | 0.444  | −16.4%  | ... W4A16 loses 1.3 points of HumanEval pass@1 and 8.7 points of GSM8K strict-match.
